subject: Amendment roadmap — capacity uplift & stepwise discount proposal
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@auroratech.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@auroratech.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Amendment roadmap — capacity uplift & stepwise discount proposal

Hi Sam and Priya,

Thanks again for the time last week — great to see AuroraTech’s usage accelerating. Per our conversation, I’ve sketched an amendment that aims to: (1) add a committed uplift for Q2–Q4, (2) provide a stepwise discount schedule that grows with sustained volume, and (3) include a short price-hold window to buy you time while procurement completes approval.

High-level proposal (draft):
- Baseline commit: 1.2M tokens / month for 12 months (adds to existing contract).
- Step discounts: 10% off list at +10% sustained uplift; 15% at +30% sustained uplift (measured quarterly).
- One-time onboarding credit: $15k applied to first invoice if commit executed by end of Q2.
- Temporary price hold: 90 days from signature for current per-token rates on newly committed volume.

I attached a first-pass amendment (Attachment: Aurora_Amendment_v1.pdf). This is intentionally concise — I want to validate the numbers and any procurement asks before sending legal a redline. Two asks from you:
1) Is the baseline commit (1.2M tokens/mo) in the right ballpark for planned Q3 workloads?
2) Would procurement require a shorter price-hold or different invoice timing?

If this looks directionally correct I’ll loop in Marissa and Ben to finalize commercial language and draft the DocuSign.

Best,
Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Attachment: Aurora_Amendment_v1.pdf (pdf, 124 KB)
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@auroratech.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@auroratech.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Amendment roadmap — capacity uplift & stepwise discount proposal

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the draft. Quick answers from our side:

1) Baseline commit: 1.2M tokens/mo is reasonable as an initial uplift; we may need to flex to 1.4M in peak months, but we can start there and true-up.
2) Procurement asks: three items
   - Can we get a 60–90 day price hold? 90 days is preferable but procurement might push for 60 to minimize their approval exposure.
   - Invoice timing: we prefer net-30 for the additional committed volume; procurement will require a PO.
   - Evidence: they’ll request a short security/compliance statement to attach to the PO (SOC 2 scope confirmation).

Also — the onboarding credit is helpful. Can the credit be applied as a contra on the first invoice rather than a separate refund? That simplifies our bookkeeping.

If you can tweak the amendment with those points I’ll share with Priya (procurement) and schedule a 30-minute sync after that.

Thanks,
Sam

--
Sam Reynolds | Head of Platform Engineering, AuroraTech
sam@auroratech.com | +1 617-555-0102
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Aurora amendment — procurement asks (action items)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Sam’s reply. Quick notes and asks:

On Sam’s three procurement asks:
- Price hold: they asked for 60–90 days, leaning 90. Recommend we offer 90-day hold on per-token rates for the newly committed volume only; existing rates remain as-is. This is time-limited and should not block legal.
- Invoice / PO: they want net-30 plus a PO. Ben — please confirm if our standard amendment supports PO-based invoicing and whether net-30 is acceptable for committed volume on an enterprise account.
- SOC2 confirmation: Marissa — can you coordinate a short one-page confirmation (we typically provide the SOC 2 scope excerpt + link to our compliance page). I’ll copy the compliance mention into the amendment.

Commercial tweaks I propose before we send v2 to Aurora:
- Make onboarding credit a contra applied to first invoice (Sam asked for this).
- Add explicit quarterly true-up clause to allow for temporary flex to 1.4M in peak months with a true-up calculation.
- Document the 90-day price hold window and make it explicit it applies only to new committed volume.

If Ben gives the OK on invoicing/net terms I’ll prepare Aurora_Amendment_v2 and the DocuSign and send to Sam/Priya. Target: have v2 to them by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Alex
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@auroratech.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@auroratech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Amendment roadmap — capacity uplift & stepwise discount proposal

Sam / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the procurement context. Attached is Aurora_Amendment_v2.docx that incorporates your asks: contra onboarding credit applied to the first invoice, explicit quarterly true-up (handles short-term 1.4M peaks), and a 90-day price-hold on newly committed volume.

Key commercial summary (v2):
- Commit: 1.2M tokens / month for 12 months on top of existing contract.
- Step discounts applied at quarterly measurement points: 10% at sustained +10% uplift; 15% at sustained +30% uplift.
- Onboarding credit: $15,000 contra to the first invoice.
- Price hold: 90 days post-signature on newly committed volume only.
- Billing: net-30; PO accepted.

Links and next steps:
- Amendment v2 attached (Attachment: Aurora_Amendment_v2.docx).
- DocuSign envelope queued: https://docusign.com/abcdef-aurora-4521 (will route to Priya for PO/approval).

Marissa will attach a short SOC 2 scope confirmation to the DocuSign packet. Ben confirmed net-30 and PO flow internally. Once you sign we’ll schedule a short onboarding checkpoint to align on expected peak windows.

If anything in v2 needs to change, flag it in the DocuSign comments and we’ll iterate quickly. Otherwise we’ll route for signature and booking.

Appreciate the collaboration — let me know if you want a 15-minute call to walk the amendment.

Best,
Alex
